utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-65-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Mejakic, Momcilo Gruban, Dusan Fustar, and Dusan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Right. May we have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ann Sutherland, Michael McVicker, Katharina Margetts, and Sebastiaan Van Hooydonk, acting case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am attorney-at-law Jovan Simic on behalf of the accused Zeljko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. May it please the court, attorney Dragan Ivetic from Chicago for Mr. Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mr. Branko Lukic for Mr. Momcilo Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Slobodanka Nedic. I'm here on behalf of Mr. Dusan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the outset I should say two things. Firstly, that I am aware that there is an application on the Rule 11 bis for this case to be transferred to another jurisdiction. That is being considered. Naturally, pending that determination, the pre-trial work must continue. The Senior Legal Officer had requested the parties to submit brief reports on matters of interest and any information that they wished to raise at the Status Conference by Wednesday, the 20th of October. So far we received a report from the Prosecution and one from the Knezevic Defence. I take it that the Defence of Mejakic and Fustar have no specific matters to raise, but if they do they will be provided with an opportunity to do so. Our first pending motion. There was the Prosecution motion on the Rules 92 bis and 89(F) and a request for protective measures. The Chamber has issued a decision in that. Then there is the Prosecution addendum to the Rules 92 bis and 89(F) motion and a decision has also been issued in response to that motion. And there is a Prosecution motion to add four witnesses and to withdraw one. And a decision has been issued. There is the Prosecution motion to amend the schedules to the indictment and today the Chamber issued a decision asking the Prosecution to clarify certain matters relating to that motion. That leaves outstanding the Prosecution's motion pursuant to Rule 68 for exempting specific material from disclosure. That just came in and requires review and further consideration. Our pre-trial briefs and Rule 65 ter filings, the pre-trial submissions are complete. As for disclosure, disclosure is complete in terms of Rule 66(A)(i) and 66(A)(ii). Rule 68, except for the motion I just mentioned, my understanding is that the Prosecution has completed its review of databases and other relevant sources and has disclosed all Rule 68 material, the last batch being disclosed to the Defence on the 20th of October. And the Prosecution informs us that there has been some progress on the electronic disclosure system. Rule 68 material is available online, including the Omarska appeal material. I have another heading here, Rule 66(B), but the applications were in fact made on the Rule 66(A)(ii) and Rule 68. And I'll tell you how I think Rule 66(B) arises when we discuss the matter. The Fustar Defence sought disclosure of material from the interview with Predrag Banovic. And that material was couriered to the Fustar Defence on the 20th of October. Now, the Knezevic Defence has sought to obtain a number of documents that it claims are in the Prosecution's custody. First, photoboards produced during the course of testimony of six named witnesses; secondly, patients' logbooks which the Defence claims were seized by the Prosecution at the Prijedor hospital; and finally the full unredacted transcripts of the appeal hearing in Kvocka, which according to the Defence contains exculpatory material. Ms. Sutherland, would you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Starting first with the photoboards, and I should say I am in receipt of your latest filing and I presume the Defence is, too. This is a filing which is dated the 22nd of October and the 21st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Defence are in possession of copies of those letters. They were addressed to them. With respect to the photo issue, one of our priorities over the last few months has been to resolve this issue and the evidentiary issues raised in Ms. Nedic's letter. We could respond to her in a piecemeal fashion but we want to do it in one substantive reply. And in that regard we need to speak with a Rule 70 provider before we can do that. A meeting is being scheduled in the next month for that to occur in a third country and after which we will be in a position to respond fully to Ms. Nedic's letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to the hospital records, Ms. Nedic's original request was a broad one in relation to the victims named in the scheduled incidents attached to the indictment. The latter request of last week was more specific. We have re-reviewed the materials and we disclosed an additional five documents on Friday, the 22nd of October. As far as the assertions that they contain exculpatory material, we have reviewed that material and disclosed those documents we deem that fall within the ambit of the rule. And unless Ms. Nedic can provide us with perhaps a list of persons in the Keraterm camp, then we will re-review the documents again. But at this stage the Prosecution is not prepared to disclose willy-nilly documents relating to patient records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The unredacted transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Omarska appeal, we disclosed on Thursday a transcript of a witness who testified in that case with a pseudonym. We have reviewed the closed session/private session materials for Rule 68, and we are of the view that the closed session -- there are no Rule 68 excerpts within the private session/closed session material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But they are seeking disclosure of the statements of all the witnesses, not just one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The transcripts are available to the Defence. The open-session transcripts are available to the Defence on the system, the electronic system, on the Internet. We have reviewed the closed session and private session transcripts, and we have -- the transcript that was disclosed in the latter part of last week related to one of our witnesses, so it was pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii), and we apologise for that oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nedic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I must confirm that I have indeed received some of the documents that I had requested. I accept that at this point in time the Prosecution cannot fully respond to our request as far as the photoboards are concerned, and I am sure they will follow the procedure in terms of disclosure of these materials. As for the medical documents, some of those documents have been forwarded to us. It is a fact that these were not the originals that we had requested and that had been seized at the Prijedor hospital, though. The OTP informed us that we should in a way prove that there should be disclosure pursuant to Rule 68. In view of paragraph 16 of the indictment where it is stated that the prisoners had no or insufficient medical care, we believe that constitutes a sufficient reason for us to request the disclosure of these documents. What this is about is that we have received some typewritten records. I am not sure if there had been a careful selection of those texts that were typewritten. This was certainly not in the order in which the patients were admitted. We are seeking to receive those that had been hand written and had been accessible at one point in time. Before the OTP seized those documents, those documents had appeared in the Omarska case as exhibits purportedly. As for these materials from the appeals hearings in the Kvocka case, it is true that we have received some documents and that the identity of those witnesses have -- has been disclosed to us, at least in as far as the Defence has so far been able to go through the documents found in our locker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I was wondering whether you have considered whether the Prosecution does not have an obligation under 66(B) to disclose some of this material which is in its possession on the basis that it is in your custody and that it is material to the preparation of the Defence. Although the Defence requested it on the 66(A)(ii). It may be that 66(B) is also applicable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this material could be construed as being material to the Defence position pursuant to Rule 66(B). However, the request was made under Rule 68 for records. It is the Prosecution's allegation that there was -- medical care was non-existent or inadequate. And from that point of view it is arguable that the Defence are interested in any records of people from the camps who were treated at the Prijedor hospital. We are erring on the side of caution because these records relate to people's personal medical records, and we did re-review the records once we had Ms. Nedic's more specific request last week. We can discuss this -- I spoke with Ms. Nedic just prior to the Status Conference a moment ago and said that we could further discuss this issue after the Status Conference this afternoon. And it may be that we can come to some sort of an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Ms. Nedic, of course you will want to consider all the possibilities that are open to you under the Rules and take whatever action is in the best interest of your client.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. We shall try to reach an agreement with the OTP on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As for the witnesses, 59 witnesses - and this is on the basis of information provided by the Prosecution - of whom nine are to be called live, ten statements and transcripts under Rule 92 bis; 40 statements and transcripts under Rule 89(F); thus a mixture of live evidence, statements, and transcripts with or without cross-examination, and on that basis the Prosecution estimates the length of the case excluding cross-examination to be four weeks. That would be quite magnificent. Is that still your estimate, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was if the motion pursuant to Rule 89(F) and Rule 92 bis was going to be granted. So in the event it's not, then that time period obviously expands greatly. The prior estimate given by Ms. Korner was six weeks, and that was excluding cross-examination, and that was under the old Rule 92 bis motion. So if neither of those motions were going to be granted, the Prosecution case, the length of the Prosecution case would be a lot greater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It may very well be that this case may be heard much earlier than you might imagine. Any other matters? Ms. Nedic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In my letter I also stated that my client asked me to start this discussion before the Trial Chamber at a Status Conference, the issue namely of counsel travelling to Prijedor in order to set up our defence because there is -- the registry has refused to compensate us financially for these travel needs. And my client believes that this severely prejudices his chances of setting up a defence. Therefore he's pressing to have these issues resolved. I have exchanged several letters with the registry with regard to this, and they -- since April they have stood by their position that the Defence would not be compensated for their travel needs to Prijedor and the carrying out of investigations there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It would then be a matter for you, Ms. Nedic, to decide what action to take in view of the stage of the discussions that you've had with the Registrar. Those matters are essentially matters for the Registrar, but the Trial Chamber will always ensure, seek to ensure the fairness of the trial. Any other matters from any of the other Defence counsel? May I then ask the accused persons whether there is anything concerning their detention or concerning the case that they would wish to raise, and I start first with Mr. Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MEJAKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no objections to the conditions at the Detention Unit. My health is relatively good. There is something else that I would like to raise, two further issues that have been brought up already in a way. One relates to the decision by the registry, a decision that has not been made yet pursuant to an Appeals Chamber ruling with regard to do with the conflict of interests regarding Mr. Jovan Simic's counsel. The Chamber has called for Mr. Simic's counsel to be revoked in two cases, the first time in this case and the other is the Kvocka case. The Registrar has still not made this decision, this ruling, therefore I am not certain that tomorrow I will still be represented by counsel before this Tribunal. The next issue, if you allow, has to do with a Prosecution proposal for my case to be transferred to a national jurisdiction, specifically back to Bosnia and Herzegovina. The procedure has already been set in motion, and I believe motions have been exchanged between the Defence team and the OTP. A special counsel has been nominated that will rule on these matters. In order not to be made a mere object of these proceedings, I would like to say the following: If I'm not mistaken, the OTP has brought charges against me before this Tribunal. A Judge of this Tribunal confirmed the indictment. 16 months ago I voluntarily surrendered to this Tribunal, convinced that I would be tried in a fair and just manner. The main reason behind my decision to surrender was to have the truth established. I am determined to give my own contribution to establishing the truth. That is the only way we can have justice for everyone. That is why I would like to ask you to please bear in mind the fact that for me this Tribunal is the only place where this can be done, where this can be achieved. I wish to be tried right here. So much from me. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mejakic. May I say in response to your first point that the matter is with the Registrar. The Registrar will, in response to the decision of the Appeals Chamber, decide on the question of Mr. Simic's representation. And it is at that stage when the Registrar has decided that you will be in a position to take any action that is necessary. In any event, I am confident that the Registrar will see to it that you are not unrepresented. But let us wait for the Registrar's decision. Now, the next matter I had adverted to in my opening remarks; that is, the Prosecution's motion to have this case transferred to another jurisdiction. I hear what you have said. As you are aware, a Chamber has been established for that specific purpose. And under the relevant rule, you will have a right to make representations, you and your counsel. So the kind of representations that you have made here today you will have an opportunity to make before that special Chamber that has been established for that purpose. So thank you very much. You may sit. Now, Mr. Fustar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED FUSTAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in relation to the conditions in the Detention Unit, I have no objections likewise. What I have to say on my behalf is I wish to be tried here because this is the Tribunal I surrendered to. I wish now to avoid repeating the very same things that have already been said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And as I indicated this is not the appropriate forum. There is a forum in which you will have an opportunity to make those representations. Mr. Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Knezevic. The only other matter is the date of the next Status Conference. And I am fixing Wednesday, the 23rd of February as the date of the next Status Conference. If there is no other matter, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.27 p.m. 23 24 25
